title: Harvest Starter Pack
description: Starter Grafana dashboard pack v0.1.0 for the Harvest workflow engine (autumn-harvest). Covers the full ADR-0001 / telemetry.rs metric catalogue as scraped through the metrics-rs adapter (MetricsRsRecorder + metrics-exporter-prometheus). Panel choices and any thresholds mentioned in panel descriptions are starter defaults, not universal SLOs — tune to your workload. Source of truth: docs/dashboards/starter-pack-v0.1.0.json in the autumn-harvest repo; alert mapping in docs/dashboards/README.md; response runbook in docs/runbooks/harvest-alerts.md.

panels.title: Workflow start rate
panels.description: New workflow executions started per second, by workflow type.

panels.title: Workflow terminal outcomes
panels.description: Terminal workflow outcomes per second (completed / failed / cancelled / timed_out / terminated / continued_as_new). Emitted exactly once per terminal outcome (issue #519).

panels.title: Workflow failure ratio
panels.description: Alert: harvest_workflow_failure_rate (docs/runbooks/harvest-alerts.md#harvest_workflow_failure_rate) Fraction of terminal executions that ended failed, per workflow type. Starter default threshold: > 10% over 5m — a starter default, not a universal SLO.

panels.title: Queue depth
panels.description: Alert: harvest_queue_backlog_growth (docs/runbooks/harvest-alerts.md#harvest_queue_backlog_growth) Pending tasks per queue. max by (queue) avoids double-counting when several worker replicas sample the same cross-shard depth. Secondary capacity signal — the schedule-to-start p99 panel is the primary page.

panels.title: Schedule-to-start latency p99
panels.description: Alert: harvest_queue_schedule_to_start_high (docs/runbooks/harvest-alerts.md#harvest_queue_schedule_to_start_high) Seconds from task eligibility to worker claim — the canonical worker-capacity SLI (issue #501). The p99 target needs set_buckets_for_metric; the avg target works on a bucket-less exporter.

panels.title: DLQ entries by shard
panels.description: Alert: harvest_dlq_growth (docs/runbooks/harvest-alerts.md#harvest_dlq_growth) Dead-letter queue depth per shard. max by (shard) avoids replica double-counting: every worker replica samples the same shard-global count. Any growth for critical workflows is page-worthy.

panels.title: Worker slot utilization
panels.description: Alert: harvest_worker_slot_saturation (docs/runbooks/harvest-alerts.md#harvest_worker_slot_saturation) Dispatch-slot utilization per slot_type (issue #531). Pair with queue depth: slots saturated AND backlog growing = worker bottleneck; slots free while backlog grows = downstream bottleneck. 90%/5m is a starter default. Charted per worker replica (each replica owns its slots), so the legend carries the instance label.

panels.title: Workflow starts by queue
panels.description: Per-queue breakdown of workflow start rate; complements the Overview start-rate panel.

panels.title: Workflow duration p50 / p99
panels.description: End-to-end workflow execution latency. Quantile targets need set_buckets_for_metric; the avg target works on a bucket-less exporter.

panels.title: Terminal outcomes by workflow
panels.description: Per-workflow terminal outcome mix (harvest.workflow.terminal, issue #519); the Overview panel shows the same counter grouped by outcome only.

panels.title: Workflow-level retries
panels.description: Workflow-level retry policy re-runs (issue #523).

panels.title: Continue-as-new rate
panels.description: Continue-as-new fork rate (harvest.workflow.continue_as_new); sustained growth means long-lived entity workflows are cycling their histories.

panels.title: History size p99 (events)
panels.description: Recorded events per execution at completion. Persistently large histories are continue-as-new candidates.

panels.title: Oversized histories (approaching cap)
panels.description: Executions whose history has crossed the warning threshold of the history cap. max by (workflow) avoids replica double-counting: each replica samples the same fleet-wide count.

panels.title: Unfinished handlers at completion
panels.description: Workflow completed while an update/signal handler was still in flight.

panels.title: Active workflows by type & state
panels.description: Live in-progress workflow population per type, split by lifecycle state (running/paused). max by (workflow, state) avoids replica double-counting: each replica samples the same fleet-wide count. A steady rise while terminal throughput stays flat signals a leak or backlog. Alert: harvest_workflow_population_leak

panels.title: Workflow execution timeouts
panels.description: Executions force-timed-out by the execution_timeout scanner (issue #243), per hour.

panels.title: Workflow chain-lifetime timeouts
panels.description: Executions force-timed-out because their chain-scoped lifetime cap (chain_execution_timeout, issue #617) elapsed across a continue-as-new chain, per hour. Distinct from the per-run execution timeout above.

panels.title: Workflow task timeouts
panels.description: Decision-cycle (workflow task) timeouts (issue #494), per hour.

panels.title: Soft SLA breaches
panels.description: Observation-only soft SLA breaches (issue #487) — the run keeps executing; emitted exactly once per breaching run.

panels.title: Non-determinism detections
panels.description: Alert: harvest_workflow_non_determinism (docs/runbooks/harvest-alerts.md#harvest_workflow_non_determinism) Replay divergences detected (issue #480). Any non-zero value after a deploy means a replay-breaking build shipped — first action: GET /api/harvest/workflows?nd_blocked=true.

panels.title: Non-determinism blocks entered
panels.description: Executions entering the non-terminal ND block (issue #603). Rolling back the offending build resumes the cohort automatically. Companion to Alert: harvest_workflow_non_determinism.

panels.title: Workflows paused
panels.description: Operator pause events (issue #383).

panels.title: Pause duration p99
panels.description: How long paused executions stay paused before resume (operator or auto-resume ceiling).

panels.title: Workflow history bloat (early warning)
panels.description: Alert: harvest_workflow_history_bloat (docs/runbooks/harvest-alerts.md#harvest_workflow_history_bloat) At-least-once early warning: fires when an execution's recorded harvest_events count first crosses history_bloat_warn_fraction * event_hard_cap (issue #704, default 75%) -- either (1) while still RUNNING, observation-only, the run keeps executing normally, or (2) in the SAME decision that also reaches the event-count hard cap and terminally fails the execution. Emitted once per crossing per run outside a rare crash-window duplicate (deliberately biased toward a duplicate over a lost-forever signal). Requires event_hard_cap to be configured for the workflow type via WorkflowHistoryPolicy; otherwise this stays flat at zero (disabled), not an outage. Discover and rank offending executions with GET /api/harvest/workflows?history_bloat_min_events=<N> or harvest workflow list --history-bloat-min-events <N>.

panels.title: Debounced start admissions
panels.description: Trigger-burst admissions collapsed by the debounce gate (issue #499). The debounce key is deliberately not a label (unbounded tenant input).

panels.title: Debounce fires
panels.description: Debounced starts actually fired by the scanner after the trailing-edge window.

panels.title: Start-throttle deferrals
panels.description: Starts deferred (never dropped) by the start throttle (issue #607). Per-key backlog is visible at GET /api/harvest/admin/start-throttle.

panels.title: Admission gate blocks
panels.description: Starts rejected by operator admission gates (issue #377).

panels.title: Admission gate bypasses (exempt producers)
panels.description: Starts relayed by producers that are exempt-by-design from an admission gate (issue #618). Currently only the outbox relay; a non-zero rate during an incident shows already-accepted in-flight work draining past the gate rather than slipping it silently.

panels.title: Quota rejections
panels.description: Fresh workflow starts rejected because a resolved per-tenant quota key was at or over its declared active-executions, history-bytes, or dead-letters cap (issue #946). Per-key usage-vs-limit is visible at GET /api/harvest/admin/quotas.

panels.title: Codec key re-encryption
panels.description: Stored harvest_events rows re-encrypted from a retired payload-codec key onto the active one by the lazy rotation sweep (issue #948). Flat at zero while GET /api/harvest/admin/codec/rotation still reports rows remaining under a retired key id means the rotation has stalled.

panels.title: Admission gates active
panels.description: Number of currently-armed admission gates. Non-zero outside an incident window deserves a look. max() collapses the identical per-replica samples of the shared gate count.

panels.title: External signals sent
panels.description: Cross-workflow signal deliveries by outcome (issue #274).

panels.title: Activity duration p99
panels.description: Activity handler latency by activity type. The p99 target needs set_buckets_for_metric; the avg target works on a bucket-less exporter.

panels.title: Activity failure rate
panels.description: Alert: harvest_activity_failure_surge (docs/runbooks/harvest-alerts.md#harvest_activity_failure_surge) Failed activity completions per second (absolute rate — the alert’s companion 5%-of-completions ratio form is readable from the Activity success ratio panel). Starter default: page above 5% of completions or > 10 failures in 5m for a critical activity.

panels.title: Activity success ratio

targets.expr: (sum by (activity, queue) (rate(harvest_activity_attempts_total{outcome="completed",queue=~"$queue"}[$__rate_interval])) or on(activity, queue) (0 * sum by (activity, queue) (rate(harvest_activity_attempts_total{queue=~"$queue"}[$__rate_interval])))) / sum by (activity, queue) (rate(harvest_activity_attempts_total{queue=~"$queue"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.description: Alert: harvest_activity_success_ratio (docs/runbooks/harvest-alerts.md#harvest_activity_success_ratio) Completed attempts / all attempts within the single harvest.activity.attempts family (issue #528). Starter default: page below 90% over 5m. The or-on()-zero guard mirrors the alert expression so a 100%-failing activity renders 0 rather than No data.

panels.title: Failed attempts by error type (top 10)
panels.description: Terminal/non-retryable per-attempt failures with error-type breakdown (issue #528). error_type values are author-shaped — kept to topk.

panels.title: Activity retry rate
panels.description: Alert: harvest_activity_retry_storm (docs/runbooks/harvest-alerts.md#harvest_activity_retry_storm) Alert: harvest_activity_retry_storm_critical (docs/runbooks/harvest-alerts.md#harvest_activity_retry_storm) Retries actually enqueued per second — the authoritative retry-storm signal. Starter defaults: ticket > 5/s, page > 20/s, both over 5m.

panels.title: Activity pause/resume actions
panels.description: Operator pause/resume actions on an activity type, counted only when the action actually changed state (issue #807). A rare-event counter, so increase() over 1h rather than a per-second rate. This is the ACTION log, not the state: a bar here means someone pulled the lever, and a flat line means nothing about whether a hold is currently in effect — read GET /api/harvest/activities for that. Pair with the activity failure-rate panel: a pause immediately after a failure spike is the intended containment response, while pauses with no preceding spike are worth asking about.

panels.title: Circuit breakers tripped
panels.description: Per-activity circuit breakers opened in the last hour (issue #369).

panels.title: Circuit breakers closed
panels.description: Circuit breakers recovered to closed in the last hour (half-open probe success or operator force-close).

panels.title: Oldest pending task age
panels.description: Age of the oldest claimable eligible task per queue (issue #501) — the fast-detection companion to the schedule-to-start p99. Companion signal for Alert: harvest_queue_backlog_growth.

panels.title: Tasks dispatched by queue
panels.description: Per-queue dispatch rate (issue #515) — confirms the live dispatch split matches configured queue weights.

panels.title: Worker slots in use / available
panels.description: Raw dispatch-slot occupancy per slot_type across the fleet (issue #531). The Overview utilization panel maps Alert: harvest_worker_slot_saturation.

panels.title: Adaptive slot tuner target
panels.description: Current tuner slot target per slot_type (issue #548) — confirms live behaviour stays inside the operator band. Per-replica series (each worker tunes its own slots), so the legend carries the instance label.

panels.title: Slot tuner decisions
panels.description: Tuner grow/shrink/hold rate. A steady stream of grow/shrink under flat load usually means the band or step size needs retuning.

panels.title: Timers started
panels.description: Durable timer starts (harvest.timer.started); a drop to zero while workflows use ctx.timer indicates a stuck scheduler or worker.

panels.title: Timer duration p99
panels.description: Durable timer fire latency from scheduled fire time.

panels.title: Schedule runs vs skipped
panels.description: Alert: harvest_schedule_missed_runs (docs/runbooks/harvest-alerts.md#harvest_schedule_missed_runs) Dispatched vs skipped schedule firings. Any skip on a required schedule is page-worthy.

panels.title: Schedule HA fire attempts
panels.description: Alert: harvest_schedule_ha_domination (docs/runbooks/harvest-alerts.md#harvest_schedule_ha_domination) claimed vs lost_race schedule-slot claims (issue #350). In a healthy N-replica deployment claims are roughly even; extreme skew signals topology misconfiguration.

panels.title: Schedules auto-paused
panels.description: Schedules auto-paused after consecutive dispatch failures (issue #360).

panels.title: Manual schedule triggers
panels.description: Manual schedule fires via trigger-now (harvest.schedule.manual_trigger) by outcome; operator-initiated, so spikes should match known interventions.

panels.title: Schedule decision write failures
panels.description: Scheduler audit-decision rows that failed to persist. Should stay at zero.

panels.title: Completion trigger fires
panels.description: Terminal-state completion triggers fired, by trigger and outcome.

panels.title: Completion trigger condition skips
panels.description: Output-guarded completion triggers (issue #810): condition-skip rate per trigger and reason. reason=condition_unmet is a resolved skip (the guard evaluated false); reason=condition_invalid means a stored guard this build cannot parse — investigate mixed-version deploys or repair the condition.

panels.title: Schedules overdue
panels.description: Alert: harvest_schedule_missed_runs (docs/runbooks/harvest-alerts.md#harvest_schedule_missed_runs) Per-schedule overdue flag (issue #696): 1 when an active schedule is past its own cadence grace (next_run_at wedged, scheduler stalled, or an HA claim that never released), 0 when healthy. Precise per-schedule detection that names the wedged schedule, replacing absence-of-runs inference. Paused / auto-paused / manual / exhausted / at-capacity schedules read 0.

panels.title: DLQ redrives
panels.description: Dead letters redriven back onto the task queue, by outcome. The Overview DLQ-entries panel maps Alert: harvest_dlq_growth.

panels.title: Tasks quarantined (poison pill)
panels.description: Tasks quarantined to the DLQ after repeated worker-process crashes (issue #367).

panels.title: Capability misses (handler not registered)
panels.description: Alert: harvest_no_capable_worker (docs/runbooks/harvest-alerts.md#harvest_no_capable_worker); Alert: harvest_capability_miss_never_offered (docs/runbooks/harvest-alerts.md#harvest_capability_miss_never_offered); Alert: harvest_capability_miss_release_sustained (docs/runbooks/harvest-alerts.md#harvest_capability_miss_release_sustained). Tasks claimed by a worker with no handler registered for that workflow/activity type (issue #804). outcome=released is the benign, self-healing signature of CAPABILITY SKEW across a queue's fleet — most often the transient window of a rolling deploy that introduces a new type; the claim is handed back for a capable peer and no execution is failed. It never pages: a sustained released rate is the separate ticket-severity rule harvest_capability_miss_release_sustained. outcome=escalated_never_offered means the task was failed on its FIRST claim without ever being offered to a peer (capability_miss_max_redeliveries=0, or a worker-session pin whose host lacks the handler) -- that is NOT evidence the fleet lacks the handler, and is the ticket-severity rule harvest_capability_miss_never_offered. outcome=escalated means one of two bounds was hit and executions ARE being failed with a no_capable_worker: reason on the execution row (no dead-letter entry is written) -- that is the page. READ THAT REASON before concluding anything about the fleet: only the budget-exhausted-with-confirmed-coverage bound supports 'NO live worker on that queue registers the handler'; the absolute release ceiling trips when coverage could NOT be confirmed, and a live, untried worker may well be capable. Distinct from the harvest.task.quarantined metric (a worker-process CRASH, issue #367) — a capability miss never increments crash strikes. NOTE: this panel is an increase() trend, so the FIRST escalation on a brand-new (queue, task_type) series reads as 0 here -- the counter is created by its first increment, already at 1, and increase() reports last-minus-first. The alert rules carry a second set-difference arm for that case; when triaging a page whose panel looks flat, trust the alert and GET /api/harvest/workflows?state=FAILED filtered on the no_capable_worker: reason.

panels.title: Workflow cache hit ratio
panels.description: Warm-cache hit ratio on the worker hot path (issue #235). A low ratio with sticky routing enabled means affinity is not landing.

panels.title: Retention deletions by workflow type
panels.description: Alert: harvest_retention_lag (docs/runbooks/harvest-alerts.md#harvest_retention_lag) Terminal-history rows deleted by the retention janitor. A sustained zero while eligible terminal history exists means retention is lagging.

panels.title: Stranded pending tasks by shard
panels.description: Eligible pending tasks with no live worker able to claim them, per shard. max by (shard) avoids replica double-counting of the shared per-shard sample. Alert: harvest_shard_undrained.

panels.title: Summary retention — summaries GC'd (issue #752)
panels.description: Execution summaries GC'd by the tiered-retention summary pass (issue #752). Distinct from the history-row retention deletions above; a sustained zero while eligible summaries exist means the summary GC is lagging.

panels.title: Rate-limit buckets — idle buckets collected (issue #1127)
panels.description: Inert per-tenant rate-limit buckets collected by the retention janitor's idle-bucket GC (issue #1127), by key family. harvest_rate_limit_buckets rows are auto-registered and were never deleted before this, so the two caller-keyed families (dyn-rate, start-throttle) grew one row per tenant forever. A flat zero while the table keeps growing means the GC is off (rate_limit_bucket_retention_secs = null) or every candidate is pinned by a live dependent — GET /admin/retention reports the per-shard count either way. The bucket key is deliberately NOT a label: it is the unbounded value this pass exists to collect.

panels.title: Dispatch rate by shard
panels.description: Per-shard task dispatch rate (issue #961). The shard-dimension twin of the per-queue dispatch panel: a multi-shard worker round-robins across its assigned shards, so a shard flatlining at 0 while siblings are busy means it is being starved or has no covering poller. Cross-check with 'Stranded pending tasks by shard'.

panels.title: Concurrency in flight (top 10 keys)
panels.description: Per-key in-flight executions against the concurrency limit (issue #247). key cardinality is author-controlled — kept to topk.

panels.title: Concurrency deferred (top 10 keys)
panels.description: Per-key starts deferred at the concurrency cap. Sustained deferrals mean the limit is the bottleneck.

panels.title: Rate-limit bucket state (top 10 keys)
panels.description: Token-bucket levels and refill rates per rate-limit key (issue #88).

panels.title: Rate-limit throttle events (top 10 keys)
panels.description: Dispatches rescheduled because a rate-limit bucket was empty.

panels.title: Latest-wins supersedes
panels.description: Running executions cancelled because a newer run superseded them under the latest-wins concurrency strategy (on_conflict = cancel_running, issue #811). The concurrency key is deliberately not a label (unbounded tenant input) — use GET /admin/concurrency for per-key detail.

panels.title: Nested admission residual over limit
panels.description: A nested self-referential completion-trigger admission (cancelling an incumbent synchronously starts a new run under the same on_conflict = cancel_running key) left the key transiently over its declared limit — the outer admission is protected from being shed, so the nested pass has nothing left it may cancel. Self-healing on the next ordinary admission for the key (issue #1197).

panels.title: Quota supersede credit not shed
panels.description: A cancel_running admission's quota check credited a candidate's usage against the incumbent it planned to shed, but the real supersede pass left that candidate running — a corrupt neighbour, a benign terminal race, or (issue #1228 review) a row locked elsewhere that the non-blocking supersede probe skipped rather than waited on. The key may stay over its declared cap until the next admission for it; alert on sustained non-zero rates.

panels.title: Payload size p99
panels.description: Observed payload sizes by payload kind (issue #252). Bridged in the metrics-rs adapter by issue #754, but the engine has no emission call sites for harvest.payload.bytes as of v0.1.0 (pre-existing issue #252 gap) — this panel stays empty until emission is wired; see the issue #754 review.

panels.title: Payload cap rejections
panels.description: Payloads rejected by the byte-cap guard (issue #252). Bridged in the metrics-rs adapter by issue #754, but the engine has no emission call sites for harvest.payload.rejected as of v0.1.0 (pre-existing issue #252 gap) — this panel stays empty until emission is wired; see the issue #754 review.

panels.title: Payloads offloaded (claim-check)
panels.description: Fields offloaded to the external PayloadStore (issue #524).

panels.title: Offload fetch latency p99
panels.description: Claim-check blob fetch latency on the replay/read path.

panels.title: Webhook deliveries
panels.description: Inbound webhook triggers received vs rejected, per registered binding path (issue #344).

panels.title: Worker session acquisitions
panels.description: Session acquisitions by outcome (acquired / timed_out / broken) — issue #606.

panels.title: Query handler duration p99
panels.description: Read-only query handler latency (issue #234).

options.content:
### Deployment preflight

**Alert: harvest_preflight_failed** — no native ADR-0001 metric exists for this check; run the management check directly or export it through your own probe with bounded labels.

Deployment readiness is failing or repeatedly warning, so new workflow starts may land on a misconfigured Harvest runtime.

**First action:**

```
harvest preflight --output json
```

**API:** `GET /api/harvest/admin/preflight`

**Runbook:** [docs/runbooks/harvest-alerts.md#harvest_preflight_failed](https://github.com/autumn-foundation/autumn-harvest/blob/trunk-dev/docs/runbooks/harvest-alerts.md#harvest_preflight_failed)

### Worker fleet coverage

**Alert: harvest_no_active_workers** — no native ADR-0001 metric exists for this check; run the management check directly or export it through your own probe with bounded labels.

Harvest has work that requires a queue or shard, but no active worker can claim it.

**First action:**

```
harvest worker health --output json
```

**API:** `GET /api/harvest/workers/health`

**Runbook:** [docs/runbooks/harvest-alerts.md#harvest_no_active_workers](https://github.com/autumn-foundation/autumn-harvest/blob/trunk-dev/docs/runbooks/harvest-alerts.md#harvest_no_active_workers)

### Worker fleet saturation

**Alert: harvest_worker_saturation** — no native ADR-0001 metric exists for this check; run the management check directly or export it through your own probe with bounded labels.

A worker fleet is present but not healthy enough to drain the queue at the expected rate. The Overview *Worker slot utilization* panel and the Queues & workers row are the closest native-metric proxies.

**First action:**

```
harvest worker list --status Active --output json
```

**API:** `GET /api/harvest/workers`

**Runbook:** [docs/runbooks/harvest-alerts.md#harvest_worker_saturation](https://github.com/autumn-foundation/autumn-harvest/blob/trunk-dev/docs/runbooks/harvest-alerts.md#harvest_worker_saturation)

### Shard readiness

**Alert: harvest_shard_unready** — no native ADR-0001 metric exists for this check; run the management check directly or export it through your own probe with bounded labels.

A shard cannot safely accept or drain workflow work, or the readiness report is partial.

**First action:**

```
harvest shard health --fail-on-unready --output json
```

**API:** `GET /api/harvest/admin/shards/health`

**Runbook:** [docs/runbooks/harvest-alerts.md#harvest_shard_unready](https://github.com/autumn-foundation/autumn-harvest/blob/trunk-dev/docs/runbooks/harvest-alerts.md#harvest_shard_unready)

### Build-routing compatibility

**Alert: harvest_no_compatible_worker** — no native ADR-0001 metric exists for this check; run the management check directly or export it through your own probe with bounded labels.

Build-aware routing is protecting replay safety, but no live worker is eligible for an execution's required build.

**First action:**

```
harvest workflow stack <execution_id>
```

**API:** `GET /api/harvest/workers/health`

**Runbook:** [docs/runbooks/harvest-alerts.md#harvest_no_compatible_worker](https://github.com/autumn-foundation/autumn-harvest/blob/trunk-dev/docs/runbooks/harvest-alerts.md#harvest_no_compatible_worker)

### Queue coverage

**Alert: harvest_queue_uncovered** — no native ADR-0001 metric exists for this check by design (a continuously-sampled gauge labeled by queue name would be unbounded cardinality for dynamically-named queues); run the management check directly or export it through your own probe with a bounded, allowlisted queue-name label.

A queue has pending work but zero live (Active or Draining) workers are polling it. Distinct from Worker fleet coverage above, which checks static, declared-required-queue coverage regardless of pending work — this alert is data-driven and fires only on real stranded work, so it also catches ad-hoc/dynamically-named queues.

**First action:**

```
harvest queue coverage --json
```

**API:** `GET /api/harvest/admin/queue-coverage`

**Runbook:** [docs/runbooks/harvest-alerts.md#harvest_queue_uncovered](https://github.com/autumn-foundation/autumn-harvest/blob/trunk-dev/docs/runbooks/harvest-alerts.md#harvest_queue_uncovered)

panels.title: Saga compensations
panels.description: Alert: harvest_saga_compensation_spike (docs/runbooks/harvest-alerts.md#harvest_saga_compensation_spike) Real compensation sequences entered (issue #801) — counted exactly once per unwind, at unwind start. A sustained rise above the workflow's baseline is the earliest downstream-outage signal: forward saga steps are failing and rolling back en masse.

panels.title: Saga compensation failures
panels.description: Alert: harvest_saga_compensation_failed (docs/runbooks/harvest-alerts.md#harvest_saga_compensation_failed) Unwinds that finished with at least one compensation error (issue #801) — the dangling-state case (HarvestError::SagaCompensationFailed). Any increase warrants a page: committed side effects were left un-rolled-back and need manual reconciliation. Distinct from harvest_workflow_terminal{outcome="failed"}.

panels.title: Activity handler panics
panels.description: Contained activity/local-activity handler panics per second (issue #782) — a `panic!()`/`unwrap()` in an `#[activity]` body caught at the dispatch boundary and converted to a retryable typed `HandlerPanic` failure. Fires once per panicking attempt (a retry that panics again increments again), so this is a per-attempt panic-rate signal distinct from ordinary `Err` failures and from process-crash quarantine (harvest_task_quarantined). A sustained rise points at a code bug in an activity, not a downstream outage.

panels.title: Workflow handler panics
panels.description: Contained workflow-body handler panics per second (issue #782) — a panic in a `#[workflow]` body caught in the executor and re-dispatched under a bounded panic-retry budget (WorkerConfig::workflow_panic_max_attempts), then failed terminally as a typed `HandlerPanic`. Emitted on every panic entry (each retry and the final terminal failure), so a workflow that panics N times before exhausting its budget emits N samples. A rise indicates a deterministic code bug on the workflow path.

panels.title: Signals received
panels.description: Signals durably delivered into workflow histories per second (issue #684). Counted at the single live-only delivery choke point; each signal is counted exactly once, never on replay.

panels.title: Unhandled signals
panels.description: Alert: harvest_signal_unhandled_rate (docs/runbooks/harvest-alerts.md#harvest_signal_unhandled_rate) Delivered signals a workflow left unconsumed when it reached a Completed/Failed terminal outcome (issue #684). Signals excused by a lost signal-or-deadline race (#476) are never counted; cancel/terminate/timeout are out of scope. A sustained rise above baseline means callers may be failing to drive the workflow.

panels.title: Updates admitted
panels.description: Workflow updates durably admitted per second (issue #684). Emitted post-commit at the single admission choke point, labeled by workflow + queue. The update name is deliberately not a label (admission is at the free-form update route boundary, before the name is resolved against a handler, so it cannot be bounded by construction); per-name visibility lives on the completed/failed/rejected panels.

panels.title: Update validator rejections
panels.description: Alert: harvest_update_rejected_rate (docs/runbooks/harvest-alerts.md#harvest_update_rejected_rate) Workflow updates rejected by their registered validator before admission (a durable pre-admission 422) (issue #684). Scope is validator rejections only. A spike usually means a client is sending malformed/stale update payloads.

panels.title: Updates completed
panels.description: Admitted workflow updates whose handler completed successfully per second (issue #684). Emitted post-commit, exactly once per completed update.

panels.title: Updates failed
panels.description: Admitted workflow updates whose handler returned an error per second (issue #684). Emitted post-commit, exactly once per failed update.

panels.title: Update latency (admit → terminal)
panels.description: Wall-clock latency from an update's durable admission (UpdateAdmitted) to its terminal result (UpdateCompleted/UpdateFailed) (issue #781). p99 needs set_buckets_for_metric on the exporter; the bucket-less avg fallback works on any install. Rejected updates are excluded (no handler runs).

panels.title: Canary round-trip latency p99

targets.expr: sum by (queue, shard) (rate(harvest_canary_roundtrip_sum{queue=~"$queue",shard=~"$shard"}[$__rate_interval])) / sum by (queue, shard) (rate(harvest_canary_roundtrip_count{queue=~"$queue",shard=~"$shard"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.description: Synthetic liveness-canary probe round-trip latency (issue #796) — wall-clock seconds from start-requested to terminal completion of the built-in throwaway workflow that exercises the live start → dispatch → activity → durable-timer → complete path, per probed (queue, shard). Distinct from the #512 replay canary (which validates code changes). The p99 target needs set_buckets_for_metric; the avg target works on a bucket-less exporter. A flatlined series means no probe has completed — a wedged pipeline for that (queue, shard).

panels.title: Canary success rate
panels.description: Synthetic liveness-canary probe completions per second per (queue, shard) (issue #796). A rate that drops to zero while the fleet looks structurally healthy (workers heartbeating, queues shallow) is the signature of a silently wedged execution pipeline — detectable within one probe interval, before any customer workflow misses its SLA. Distinct from the #512 replay canary.

panels.title: Canary failures
panels.description: Synthetic liveness-canary probe failures per second per (queue, shard) (issue #796) — a probe that did not reach terminal completion within its per-probe timeout, or terminated in a non-completed state. A sustained rise on one (queue, shard) isolates a wedged worker pool or a write-blocked shard. Distinct from the #512 replay canary.

panels.title: Mutex acquire wait p99
panels.description: Wall-clock time a workflow waited to acquire a durable mutex, from request (enqueued as a FIFO waiter) to grant (issue #691). p99 needs set_buckets_for_metric on the exporter; the bucket-less avg fallback works on any install. The lock key is deliberately not a label (ADR-0001 §7) — high cardinality.

panels.title: Mutex held duration p99
panels.description: Wall-clock time a durable mutex was held, from grant to release (drop / explicit / terminal sweep / lease reclaim) (issue #691). Long holds serialize contenders and are the first thing to check when acquire waits climb. p99 needs set_buckets_for_metric; the avg fallback works on any install.

panels.title: Mutex contention depth
panels.description: FIFO waiter-queue length for a durable mutex key at the moment of the last grant (contention depth, issue #691). A sustained rise means workflows are queueing on a hot lock key — combine with the held-duration panel to find long-held locks. The lock key is deliberately not a label (ADR-0001 §7).

panels.title: Paused queues (dispatch held)
panels.description: Alert: harvest_queue_paused_too_long (docs/runbooks/harvest-alerts.md#harvest_queue_paused_too_long) 1 while an operator hold is in effect on a queue, 0 otherwise (issue #619). max by (queue) avoids double-counting when several worker replicas sample the same fleet-wide pause. Pair with the queue-depth and oldest-pending-age panels: a rising backlog WITH this at 1 is a deliberate hold, not a capacity incident — the single most common false page during an outage freeze.

panels.title: Connector messages received
panels.description: Messages pulled from each broker binding (issue #944). A flat line while lag climbs means the consumer is stuck, not idle.

panels.title: Connector dispatch outcomes
panels.description: Per-binding dispatch outcome (issue #944): dispatched / idempotent_replay / deferred / dead_lettered / retried. A rising `retried` share is harvest-side failure, not a bad message.

panels.title: Connector poison messages
panels.description: Messages quarantined to a dead-letter destination (issue #944), by reason: malformed / mapping_rejected / target_rejected. Triage with `SELECT binding, reason, count(*) FROM harvest_connector_dead_letters GROUP BY 1,2`.

panels.title: Connector consumer lag
panels.description: Unconsumed backlog per binding where the broker client exposes it (issue #944), measured as work still owed to the consumer rather than immediately fetchable: Kafka high watermark minus the committed offset (clamped up to the low watermark, so retention-deleted records are excluded); SQS ApproximateNumberOfMessages plus ApproximateNumberOfMessagesNotVisible (a message abandoned for retry is not visible, so the visible count alone drains toward zero during an outage). Every replica reports the same number -- SQS reads whole-queue depth, and the Kafka sample is group-wide across the topic's partitions rather than the replica's own assignment -- so `max by` deduplicates replicas without under-reporting either adapter.

panels.title: Scanner tick rate
panels.description: Liveness heartbeat rate of each background control loop (issue #797). Every loop ticks on EVERY iteration, including no-work iterations, so a series that flat-lines to zero means that loop is wedged (panicked, deadlocked, or stalled on a never-returning query) -- not merely idle. Kept per-instance deliberately: every replica runs its own copy of all seven loops, so summing across instances would let a healthy replica mask a wedged one. Note `retention` polls hourly by default, so at short rate intervals its line sits indistinguishably near zero when healthy -- judge it on the 3h panel beside this one, whose window is longer than the janitor's cadence. Alert: harvest_scanner_stalled. Bounded `scanner` label (7 values); execution.id is never a label (ADR-0001 SS7).

panels.title: Scanner ticks (3h)
panels.description: Iterations completed per loop over 3h (issue #797) -- the low-frequency companion to the rate panel, and the panel to judge `retention` on. The window is deliberately LONGER than the slowest loop's cadence: the janitor polls hourly by default, so any window under an hour legitimately contains zero increments for much of every healthy hour and the "zero means wedged" reading would be false exactly where it is supposed to be authoritative. At 3h a healthy janitor floors at ~3. A series that stops incrementing is the wedge signal -- note that on the log axis a zero reads as a BREAK in the line rather than a dip to the baseline. The axis is log because a sub-second loop contributes ~21,600 ticks over the same window against the janitor's ~3, and a linear scale would pin retention indistinguishably to zero -- the exact illegibility this panel exists to fix. Retune alongside the alert's 3h window if you have changed the retention tick interval. Per-instance so one replica's wedged loop is not hidden by its healthy peers. A multi-shard worker runs one timeout/poison_pill/pause_auto_resume loop PER SHARD under one label, and the metric carries no shard label -- to catch a single-shard wedge use the scanner_liveness check in GET /admin/preflight, which names the wedged instance's shard.

panels.title: Measured RPO (seconds of acknowledged work a failover would lose)
panels.description: Alert: harvest_replication_lag_high (docs/runbooks/harvest-alerts.md#harvest_replication_lag_high) The RPO per shard. A MISSING series means the RPO is UNKNOWN, not zero — no standby, no slot, or a standby further behind than the retained watermark trail. Pair with the connected-standbys panel: this one says 'slow', that one says 'down'.

panels.title: Connected standbys (0 = replication is DOWN)
panels.description: Alert: harvest_replication_down (docs/runbooks/harvest-alerts.md#harvest_replication_down) Live walsenders per shard. 0 means DR is not protecting that shard: the RPO is unbounded and growing, and the lag panel above is silent rather than alarming, which is why this is the 'replication is broken' signal.

panels.title: WAL backlog
panels.description: Worst-case WAL bytes a standby has not consumed. Survives a disconnected standby (a slot pins WAL with no walsender), so it stays real when the time lag is unknowable — and it is the disk-pressure signal for an abandoned slot.

panels.title: Shard write-authority generation (watch for SKEW)
panels.description: The fencing epoch each shard's database reports. The value is uninteresting; the SKEW is the point — shards fail over independently, so lines at different heights mean a half-failed-over cluster.

panels.title: Workers fenced (never self-healing)
panels.description: Alert: harvest_shard_fenced (docs/runbooks/harvest-alerts.md#harvest_shard_fenced) Workers that stopped because their pinned generation was superseded. Expected for the old fleet during a planned failover; outside one it means a generation was bumped on a healthy shard. Recovered only by restarting the fleet — never by re-pinning a worker.

panels.title: Replication observable (0 = the other DR panels are STALE)
panels.description: Alert: harvest_replication_unobservable (docs/runbooks/harvest-alerts.md#harvest_replication_unobservable) Whether this shard's replication views can be read at all — usually a GRANT pg_monitor question. Read this panel FIRST: a Prometheus gauge keeps exporting its last value, so while this is 0 the RPO, standby-count and backlog panels above are frozen at their last healthy reading rather than reflecting reality.

panels.title: Audit export lag (oldest unshipped audit record)
panels.description: Alert: harvest_audit_export_lag_high (docs/runbooks/harvest-alerts.md#harvest_audit_export_lag_high) Age in seconds of the OLDEST audit record the SIEM sink has not acknowledged, per shard. This is the compliance signal: a rising line means privileged-action logs are not reaching the SIEM, and the cursor is deliberately held rather than advanced past the failure, so nothing is lost — only late. A flat 0 means every audit record on the shard is acknowledged. A MISSING series means no exporter is running for that shard at all (check GET /admin/audit-export's sink_configured), which is worse than a high value, not better.

panels.title: Audit records exported (acknowledged by the sink)
panels.description: Rate of audit records the sink acknowledged, per shard — counted only after the export cursor actually advanced, so this is a delivery rate, not an attempt rate. Delivery is at-least-once, so a redelivered batch counts again; receiver-side (shard, seq) accounting is the completeness proof, not this counter. Pair with the lag panel: throughput at zero while lag climbs is a sink outage; both healthy is a working export.

panels.title: Audit export observed (0 = the lag panel above is STALE)
panels.description: Alert: harvest_audit_export_unobservable (docs/runbooks/harvest-alerts.md#harvest_audit_export_unobservable) Whether the exporter could read this shard's cursor and lag this tick — a connection it cannot acquire, a failed cursor read, or a failed lag query all report 0. Read this panel FIRST: a Prometheus gauge keeps exporting its last value, so while this is 0 the lag panel above is frozen at its last reading rather than reflecting reality.

panels.title: RPO known (0 = readable but unmeasurable)
panels.description: Alert: harvest_replication_rpo_unknown (docs/runbooks/harvest-alerts.md#harvest_replication_rpo_unknown) Whether this shard's measured RPO has a source at all. 0 means the replication views are readable and a standby is connected, but no DR slot has confirmed a position and the standby has not reported a replay_lag either — the RPO gauge is withheld rather than published as a stale or fabricated number.
